The literature research identified the STM-32 Nucleo 144 board as a major component, operating in unison with 5 G technology for remote operations. Highlighting the advantages of these improvements, the proposed research envisions a future where robotic arms respond with cognitive grasp, changing healthcare delivery. The proposed research extends to prospective remote surgeries, connecting additional input/output devices for greater control, and concrete increases in success rates and accuracy proven through real-world data analysis. Contributing to the growth of robotic arm technology in healthcare, this work prepares the way for a paradigm change, where precision, adaptability, and soft holding moments, directed by EMG sensor input, take center stage in redefining the landscape of medical treatments.

articleTitle: Optimizing Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) Communication Efficiency with KNN-based Dynamic Time slot Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: In the continually evolving field of vehicular communications, the efficient allocation of time slots for Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication is of utmost importance. This work introduces a novel approach that employs a K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm to allocate time slots in NR V2X sidelink communications. The allocation is specifically tailored to dynamically adjust to the current density of traffic in real-time. The efficacy of the KNN-based time slot allocation system is assessed through simulating the V2X environment, encompassing a fleet of vehicles. The efficacy of the suggested methodology is assessed in relation to a random allocation technique and it is observed that the suggested strategy notably enhances allocation efficiency, slot utilization, contention window, and communication time. The findings illustrate the capacity of a KNN-based dynamic allocation system to adapt to different levels of traffic congestion, leading to the efficient utilization of network resources and the mitigation of communication latency. Furthermore, the examination of the implementation of priority queues in the allocation process is explored, resulting in enhanced efficiency of the system in scenarios involving a substantial amount of traffic.

articleTitle: Building Tomorrow: Navigating Sustainable Construction with Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: In the realm of modern architecture and construction projects, a multitude of factors weigh heavily on designers, driving them to make intricate and challenging decisions. These factors encompass the imperative to curtail energy consumption, manage resources efficiently, incorporate eco-friendly materials, harness an array of contemporary technologies, and navigate the intricate, multi-branch nature of architectural and construction endeavors. The work at hand seeks to unveil a spectrum of project tools that are currently in use within the construction industry, facilitating sustainable building design analysis. Additionally, it offers a panoramic view of the potential applications of artificial intelligence methodologies and tools, including Knowledge-Based Engineering (KBE), fuzzy logic, neural networks, and genetic algorithms. These innovative approaches can substantially enhance the early stages of design by streamlining decision making processes and optimizing both the design phase and the overall project. This article expounds upon the prospective avenues for the development and broader implementation of AI techniques in sustainable building construction, with a strong emphasis on their commercial viability.

articleTitle: Designing Advanced Motor Bearing of Electric Vehicles (EVs) Through Applying Circular Surface Texturing and Surface Engineering Methods of Cluster Magnetorheological Finishing (CMRF) and Laser Surface Hardening (LSH)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: Motor bearing is a crucial part in electric vehicles (EVs) due to its critical function of supporting the output shaft to be able to transmit loads and rotate smoothly. As the electric motor in EVs operating in a harsh environment that experience high temperatures, pressures, and rotational speeds, considering design an appropriate motor bearing that can withstand these severe conditions is needed. Proper selections of bearing type, bearing material, lubricant and surface engineering methods if needed, would lead to a successful motor bearing that can operate effectively under the extreme operating conditions of electric motor. One efficient and common type of ball bearings is the deepgroove ball bearing, which has the advantages of a fast rotation in a minimal friction, a small contact area, and a high sealability to afford harsh conditions. Silicon nitride ceramics and AISI 52100 chrome steel were found to be the most appropriate materials that exhibit various properties that a motor bearing desires to have, such as high hardness, low friction and other properties related to tribology. An efficient lubricating grease, UCON OSP-32 base fluids polyalkylene glycol (PAG), was chosen due to its characteristics of high-temperature and chemical stability, low volatility, and good electrical insulation. To ensure the best performance of the motor bearing, the circular surface texturing technique and two surface engineering methods, cluster magnetorheological finishing (CMRF) and laser surface hardening (LSH), were applied to the bearing balls and races. Because of the careful selectins of bearing type, material types, lubricant and the surface modification methods, the design of the motor bearing has met several sustainability objectives, including increasing efficiency, mitigating environmental risks, decreasing weight, and reducing waste.

articleTitle: A Global Perspective on Tourism and Hospitality Education and SDG 4: A Bibliometric Exploration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: The United Nations (UN) launched 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) in 2015 to safeguard society, the environment, and underwater and overland living beings to provide a better tomorrow. SDG 4’s mission is to provide quality education at the macro- and meso-levels that can help establish harmony and offer the opportunity to earn a livelihood. This study used the Scopus database to identify research already conducted on SDG 4 in the tourism and hospitality industry. A bibliometric analysis using the R-tool was used to study the publication patterns, author contributions, trending keyword identification, dominant countries, major affiliations, and citation analysis. It was observed that out of 353 related papers, only 97 were published since 1989 before the launch of the SDG 2030 agenda. “Green, circular, bio economy: A comparative analysis of sustainability avenues”, published in the “Journal of Cleaner Production” got maximum citations of 391. “Sustainability (Switzerland)” has published a maximum of 37 articles in the relevant area, and the USA published a maximum of 24 articles $(6.8 \%$ of total contribution) on the topic of global concern. Moreover, for a better bibliometric study, more papers in the relevant field are required, but highlighting facts of quality tourism and hospitality education to society is an initiative taken by researchers.

articleTitle: Review of Semantic Segmentation by Using Deep learning methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: Semantic segmentation, a critical task in computer vision, involves pixel-level classification of images to assign each pixel to a specific semantic category. Over the years, numerous authors have extensively explored and applied semantic segmentation techniques across diverse domains. This paper provides a brief overview of the highlights of its prominent role in advancing image understanding. Authors have proposed several pioneering architectures specifically tailored for semantic segmentation. The subsequent years saw the development of variants such as SegNet and Deep Lab, each addressing unique challenges in semantic segmentation tasks. Semantic segmentation finds applications in diverse fields, including medical imaging, autonomous vehicles, and augmented reality. Authors have demonstrated its utility in tasks such as tumor detection, road scene understanding, and object recognition, showcasing its versatility and potential societal impact. Recent trends include the integration of semantic segmentation with other computer vision tasks, such as instance segmentation and panoptic segmentation. Authors are exploring methods for improving interpretability, robustness to domain shifts, and efficiency in resource-constrained environments.

articleTitle: A Review on Facial Emotion Recognition of Subjects Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: The process of recognizing human emotion is called emotion recognition. The degree to which people can accurately identify the emotions of others varies greatly. The field of study on using technology to assist individuals in recognizing emotions is still in its infancy. The significance of facial emotion recognition lies in its ability to assist computers in deciphering human emotions from our faces. Its relevance can be summed up as follows: it can aid with mental health, make technology friendlier and more helpful, and even enhance products like video games and manufacturing processes. This approach analyzes facial expressions and characteristics using computer vision techniques to determine emotions. Commonly accepted basic emotion categories include happiness, anger, fear, disgust, and surprise. Ensuring optimal functionality of the technology for users from diverse backgrounds.

articleTitle: Classification of Maternal Health Risk Factors Using Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: Maternal health is an important issue that affects millions of women globally. Pregnancy and delivery difficulties are known to be preventable and result in the death of the majority of pregnant women. Early detection of maternal health risk factors can lead to better results for both the mother and the child. The goal of this study is to use clinical data to develop a machine-learning model that will classify risk factors for maternal health. In our work, we train the model using a dataset of patient records that includes information on medical history, demographics, and pregnancy outcomes. The most significant risk variables for maternal health were identified, and the effectiveness of many machine learning risk factor classification algorithms for mothers’ health was assessed. In this study, we categorize the risk factor levels using a variety of supervised learning algorithms, such as the K Nearest Neighbors Classifier, Decision Tree Classifier, Random Forest Classifier, GaussianNB Classifier, and SVM Classifier. We got the highest ${9 8 \%}$ accuracy for Random Forest and the lowest $91 \%$ accuracy for KNN ${9 7 \%}$ for Decision Tree and ${9 4 \%}$ and ${9 3 \%}$ for SVM and GaussianNB respectively. The investigation’s findings will provide significant new knowledge regarding the factors that increase the risk to maternal health. Using machine learning techniques, this study will also help with the classification of maternal health risk factors.

articleTitle: Supervised Machine Learning Approaches to Identify the False and True News from Social Media Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: The increasing number of online communities and social platforms like Twitter and Facebook has facilitated a level of information sharing never before seen in human history Consumers are generating and sharing more data than ever before thanks to the proliferation of social media platforms, and some of it is deceptive and has no basis in reality. Automatically determining whether a text contains misleading data or misinformation is difficult. Before passing judgment on the accuracy of a piece, even a subject matter specialist needs to look into a number of different angles. Here, this research presents machine learning strategies for distinguishing between false and genuine news. In this study, we have collected data by web scraping and employed several different techniques to train a collection of machine learning algorithms and then compare how well they perform on our datasets. In this work five machine learning algorithms have been applied to find the best algorithms. After evaluating the model, the research found that the decision tree achieved the best ${9 9. 8 4 \%}$ model accuracy from this study.

articleTitle: A Review on the Various Methods for Classifying Skin Cancer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: Skin cancer, a pervasive threat to global health, prompts a critical need for enhanced diagnostic accuracy Conventional methods relying on image segmentation struggle with the intricate diversity in sizes and shapes of skin lesions Our study introduces an innovative automated system that integrates diverse techniques, strategically selecting optimal features to refine diagnostic precision for skin cancer. Utilizing four pre-trained transfer learning Convolutional Neura Network (CNN) models-DenseNet121, ResNet50, VGG16, and ResNet18-the framework rigorously evaluates classification accuracy with a comprehensive skin dataset. Further refining accuracy, the study incorporates preprocessing steps and explores simulation parameters such as epochs, batch size, and optimizers. Meticulous analyses reveal that the most favorable accuracy outcomes are achieved with the proposed ResNet50 and ResNet18 models, particularly with a batch size of 32 coupled with the SGD optimizer. Beyond technical findings, this research marks a profound shift toward the automation of diagnostic processes, striving for error-free outcomes and emphasizing the transformative potential of deep learning models in dermatology. The integration of these models not only enhances diagnostic efficiency but also underscores potentia cost-effectiveness in healthcare, contributing to a broader discourse on leveraging technology to reshape medical diagnostics and setting a precedent for future research endeavors aimed at revolutionizing healthcare practices.

articleTitle: Secondary Batteries for Sustainable Energy: A Comprehensive Review of the Indian Landscape
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: This research paper presents an exhaustive exploration of the evolving landscape of battery technologies in the context of India’s dynamic energy ecosystem. The study evaluates the intricate interplay of factors such as manufacturing, policy frameworks, and market dynamics. As India pursues renewable energy goal of 450 GW by 2030, challenges from renewable intermittency are addressed by battery energy storage, especially Lithium-ion, playing a crucial role in grid stability. the operational energy storage capacity is currently at 20 MW, with an additional 1.3 GW in various development stages. Critical insights are provided into India’s initiatives, including the Battery Swapping Policy and the FAME (Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Electric Vehicles) Scheme. The paper explores the growing momentum in establishing battery cell manufacturing units across India and reducing dependence on imports through the National Program on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage. While certain regulations such as the Batteries Management and Handling Rules (2001) exist, the lack of comprehensive policy support underscores the need for a sustainable recycling infrastructure to facilitate circular economy and environmentally sustainable waste management practices. This comprehensive review offers a holistic understanding of the present battery landscape in India and propounds future perspectives crucial for steering the nation towards sustainable energy reliance.

articleTitle: Spatial-Economic Analysis for Optimal Electric Vehicle Charging Station Placement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: The ongoing advances in the electromobility sector, together with increased research efforts in alternative fuel technologies and growing environmental concerns, highlight the necessity and inevitability of shifting away from internal combustion engines and toward electric cars (EVs). However, in order to facilitate and accelerate the broad adoption of EVs, the apprehension of depleting battery power before reaching the next available charging station must be overcome. The present increase in electric vehicle adoption worldwide needs the creation of a well-developed charging infrastructure comprised of a significant number of charging stations. Hence, this study aims to contribute to the research community by creating an open source dataset designed to aid the experiments of researchers in the community related to the optimal placement of electric vehicle charging stations. Furthermore, we also assess and compare several prominent artificial intelligence algorithms on the dataset that we curated for Germany. Our code: https://gitlHib.coni/akaiish12/data-science-Optimal-EV-station-placement

articleTitle: Integrating IQ and Emotional Intelligence for Students Career Decision Making Using Machine Learning: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: The goal of developing a system that can accurately predict a student’s IQ and EI using a variety of data points, such as academic success, scores on aptitude tests, certifications, and feedback from professors and family members, is to design a student assessment model based on intelligence quotient using machine learning. This approach could be used to enhance student placement and guarantee career success for graduates. In addition to the foregoing, my work is important because it represents one of the initial initiatives to apply machine learning to create a comprehensive indicator of student intelligence. Although this is a difficult task, it has the ability to completely change how we evaluate kids and assist them in realizing their potential. Overall, a student assessment model based on intelligence quotient might be created utilizing a variety of different machine learning techniques. The ideal strategy will change based on the application’s particular requirements and the data’s accessibility. My task is to use machine learning to create an intelligence-based student assessment model. The placement of students can therefore be improved, and this information can be used to guarantee that students succeed in their jobs. The conclusion drawn from the foregoing is that applying machine learning to enhance student evaluation is of growing interest.

articleTitle: Automatic building detection and recognition of rooftops using convolutional neural networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: In this innovative investigation, the vital realm of automatic structure detection and reconstruction takes the spotlight, showcasing its paramount significance across remote sensing and computer vision domains. The prowess of convolution neural networks (CNNs) takes center stage as a potent tool for identifying buildings and discerning intricate roof shapes. The pivotal workflow encompasses the creation of a meticulously curated training dataset, the architecture of a proficient model, the precise segmentation of photographs, the adept localization of buildings, and the acumen to discern diverse roof configurations. As a preliminary step, a CNN is adeptly trained to classify urban elements spanning trees, roads, and structures. Subsequently, distinct roof shapes are astutely categorized as fat, gable, and hip, each representing a unique architectural facet. Leveraging the CNN’s adeptness anew, the evaluation benchmarks substantiate the efficacy of this proposed methodology, boasting remarkable success rates of $97\%$ for detection and an impressive $92\%$ for recognition processes, respectively

articleTitle: A Hybrid Segmentation Method BCOT for Skin Lesion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: Skin cancer is a widespread disease that has the potential to be life-threatening, making early detection decisive for effective treatment. The biopsy method is the formal approach employed for diagnosing skin cancer, which is highly uncomfortable and a time-intensive procedure. This research work proposes a comprehensive approach to the detection of skin cancer, integrating advanced digital image processing techniques for easy identification of cancer. A Multi-filter Fusion and Equalization technique (MFE) is proposed in the pre-processing step to enhance the image quality by removing noise and highlighting relevant features in Digital Dermoscopic (DD) images. A boundary contrast-based Otsu threshold method (BCOT) is proposed for segmentation, ensuring precise delineation of lesion boundaries. In the feature extraction phase, the grey-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) method is deployed to capture relevant textural information. GLCM captures details about how intensity values are distributed with each other. To classify various types of skin cancers, a Support Vector Machine (SVM) is leveraged in the classification step for differentiation among cancer types. The proposed method isolates the given image into malignant melanoma or benign melanoma. The experimental results are obtained based on the dataset, which is available on the public database comprising 600 images of malignant type and benign type diseases sourced from the International Skin Imaging Collaboration (ISIC) 2020. Sixty percent of the images were allocaied for training the model, while the remaining forty percent were designated for testing purposes. The presented approach attains a precision level of 97.92%. The software used for this study is MATLAB R2023b version

articleTitle: Prediction of Performance-Emission Profile with Varying Nozzle Injection Pressures of a Diesel–Biodiesel Fueled Diesel Engine by Adopting Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: Ever increasing oil price, continuous accumulating greenhouse gases and swift depleting mineral resources due to the incriminating extraction of fossil resources catches the researcher’s attention to look at alternative fuels to serve the abrupt increasing energy demands. Despite the problems like low calorific value, high density, etc., biodiesels are sustainable, renewable, and promising alternative fuel for CI engines. Adding an oxygenated additive to the biodiesel helps in reducing the harmful pollutants such as NOx which have a significant impact on ecological system and human health. In this regard, the present inquisition is aimed to study the performance-emission profiles with varying nozzle injection pressures on a direct injection diesel engine with fish oil biodiesel using Isobutanol (5%) as an additive. An ANN meta model has been prepared based on the experimental data to map input and output parameters accurately. The posed model yielded its perception with a MSE of 0.000081, MAPE of 1.978% and regression of 0.9959.

articleTitle: An Ensemble Method for Encountering Bogus News in Social Media: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: Rapid spread of the Internet Fake news travels from multiple sources to consumers via a complex ecology of websites, social media, and bots, and social media also spreads leading to changes in people’s news consumption. from multiple sources Most individuals spread bogus news to achieve popularity on social networks. This article describes an innovative hybrid fake news detection system that combines convolutional neural networks (CNN), language networks, and knowledge-based networks. We measured model performance using F1 score, precision, accuracy, and recall. Most machine learning algorithms can recognize bogus news on social media One of the most well-liked machine-learning methods for identifying false news is the use of Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and neural networks. Some of the most prevalent characteristics that may be used to detect false news include the source of the news, the language utilized, and the words used. The best technique to recognize false news depends on the unique dataset and application. A summary is a brief overview of the system, which then utilizes machine learning to identify news pieces as false or legitimate. This study is expected to be more accurate than standard ways of identifying false news. It is used to extract information from news items and the apply machine learning to categorize them as false or authentic.

articleTitle: Enhanced Skin Cancer Detection and Classification using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: Skin cancer is a major health concern for society, as it can be delicate for dermatologists to diagnose due to the similarity in appearance of numerous skin cancer colours. Beforehand discovery of lesions is pivotal for complete cure of skin cancer. Fortunately, significant progress has been made in developing automated tools to help dermatologists in the opinion of skin cancer. Artificial intelligence-supported tools have allowed for the use of a vast collection of images of lesions and benign blisters approved by histopathology. presently, the first step for a dermatologist in relating whether a skin lesion is nasty or benign is to perform a skin vivisection, which can take up to a week or further to gain a report. This design provides a predictive model employing computer-backed opinion to reduce the time gap to just a few days. Using photos of outlier lesions, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is used to categorise nine different forms of skin cancer. Millions of people could benefit greatly from this saving in time. A userfriendly website created in order to make this technology available to the general population. Dermatologists can input patient demographic data together with a photograph of a skin lesion. Also, the model will analyse the data and provide results in a matter of seconds. To ensure a broader demographic can pierce the tool, an introductory infographic runner will be developed that provides a general overview of carcinoma and instructions on how to use the online tool to gain results. Overall, this design has the implicit to make a significant positive impact on the early discovery and treatment of skin cancer, and its availability to the public will help ensure that everyone has access to dependable and effective skin cancer opinion.

articleTitle: The Impact of the Mixed Load Model on the Placement and Sizing of Distributed Generation (DG) in a Radial Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: Distribution systems heavily employ Distributed Generators (DG) to decrease losses. Some writers have explored this crucial optimization problem with a constant power load model. Consumers in distribution network load centres utilize varied loads based on voltage. A few authors have investigated this optimization problem with voltage-dependent load models. Some studies used a single load model independent of voltage or depending on bus system voltage. Few studies have employed a single load model on the whole feeder, lateral or sub-lateral, to analyze all voltage-dependent load models. A mixture of voltage-dependent load models calculates consumer load on a bus or all buses in actual distribution networks. Combining all voltage-dependent load models at one or more buses has yet to be fully researched. This study examines mixed load model effects in radial distribution networks with DG. DG position and capacity must be optimized to decrease power losses, a tough, nondifferentiable, non-convex combinatorial task. A quantum-inspired evolutionary metaheuristic algorithm solves this combinatorial optimisation challenge. A quantum-inspired evolutionary algorithm (AQiEA) determines DG placement and capacity. The suggested technique is evaluated on two IEEE benchmark test bus systems. Tabulated findings show that AQiEA reduces power loss the most.

articleTitle: Enhancing Power System Security: Neural Network Approaches for Quick and Robust Static Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: In the modern era, sophisticated techniques for ranking and screening contingencies are necessary for the efficient operation of power systems. The Multi-Layer FeedForward Neural Network (MFNN) and the Radial Basis Function Network (RBFN) are the two artificial neural networks used by the Power System Static Security Evaluation (PSSSE) module. Two indices—the line stability index and the fast voltage stability index - that are derived from NewtonRaphson Load Flow (NRLF) analysis under different load scenarios during $\mathrm{N}-1$ line outage contingency is used to determine the system’s severity. The proposed MFNN and RBFN models use load scenarios, N-1 line outage scenarios, and power system operational states as input features to train the neural network models. Predicting weighted composite indices for undetermined network environments and ranking them for security evaluation are the primary objectives. Through simulation results, the suggested PSSSE module’s robustness and performance are verified on a typical IEEE 30bus test system. The proposed model is rapid, precise, and dependable for evaluating power system static security in the event of unforeseen network conditions, according to a comparison of accuracy and execution time with NRLF analysis. The outcomes show that the MFNN and RBFN model-based designed PSSSE module is suitable for online implementation and offers a trustworthy way to evaluate the security of power systems in real-time.

articleTitle: Classifying and Predicting Covid-19 during pregnancy using RNN and ML Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: The most recent threat which was threatening every individual’s health nowadays was the Covid-19 virus. Hence focusis made on applying AI methods to predict and diagnose the covid during pregnancy. The evolution of specific recognition techniques and a lack of accurate viral identification was the main reason for the rise of Covid-19. Numerous alignment free techniques for identifying the viral infection were considered. However, all those techniques seem to be time consuming. Hence the researchers proposed alignment-free techniques by incorporating genomic methods. Numerous AI techniques were employed for gathering the mutation data, analyzing, and classifying the genome sequences, and for the preventive methods of vaccine drugs. Even though the approach tends to be effective and flexible, its difficulty lies in the process of data collection and needs proper validation. The artificial neural networks tools were used to overcome the challenges associated with Covid-19. For analyzing and evaluating, specific medical data were applied in each stage for better performance.

articleTitle: A Review of Advancements in Facial Emotion Recognition and Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: Nowadays, Emotion recognition and detection technology are trending among researchers. Automatically recognizing facial emotions is a challenging task in computer vision a face picture has a wide range of potential applications, including security while driving, interaction between humans and computers, healthcare, psychology, video conferencing cognitive research, and others. In this study, a deep-learning-based method is recommended to assess a person’s expressions with their faces. While these emotions are extremely complicated and hard for robots to comprehend, they are simple to comprehend for humans. This FER will used in lie detection by analyzing the micro-facial emotions of humans it will predict the accurate result. By using deep learning and CNN methods it can detect automatically in a real-time environment from human facial expressions. We can implement deep learning to develop robust and reliable systems. The FER is capable of recognizing and detecting facial expressions automatically. It involves training in convolutional neural networks to analyze them and examine the classification of facial emotions. The result of the dataset will depend on the specific application and the desired model accuracy. Some of the most popular and well-regarded datasets for facial expression recognition include AffectNet, FER-2013, JAFFE, CK+, and DISFA. However because they haven’t considered the difficulties presented by variations in head position, their usefulness is limited, and the accuracy still falls short of expectations. The work focused on methods and datasets that will be used to predict all kinds of such as joy, sorrow, rage, contempt, indifference, surprise, etc. And also this review provides brief information about the working methods of FER and evaluates the future challenges. This review influence will increase the efficiency of user experiences in applications like educational software, virtual assistants, and entertainment. It provides highly accurate results.

articleTitle: Offline Signature Verification with AutoencoderCNN Hybrid Feature Extraction for Improved Fake Signature Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: A novel approach aimed at elevating the performance of offline signature verification systems by harnessing the combined power of Autoencoders and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Our evaluation encompassed Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Gaussian Temporal Rule, Probabilistic Neural Networks, Multi-layered Perception, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and various combinations thereof. Notably, our proposed Autoencoder with Convolutional Neural Networks (AE with CNN) outshone all other approaches, achieving an impressive accuracy rate of $98.48 \%$. While CNN displayed commendable performance at $89 \%$, KNN and SVM fusion attained $78.50 \%$ accuracy, suggesting room for improvement in distinguishing genuine and forged signatures. The Gaussian Temporal Rule proved robust, with an accuracy of $91.20 \%$, and Probabilistic Neural Networks and Multi-layered Perception with SVM reached accuracies of $92.06 \%$ and $91.67 \%$, respectively The introduction of LSTM in conjunction with SVM and KNN significantly enhanced accuracy to $95.40 \%, 95.20 \%$, and $92.70 \%$, respectively. Collectively, these findings provide valuable insights into the potential of AE with CNN as a leading solution for achieving highly accurate signature verification, particularly in contexts where the distinction between authentic and counterfeit signatures is critical.

articleTitle: Enhancing MR Perfusion Analysis: Advanced Multi-Echo Time Tuning and Contrast-to-Noise Ratio
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Social and Sustainable Innovations in Technology and Engineering (SASI-ITE)
abstract: This paper presents theoretical and simulation-based evidence to challenge the conventional approach in the study of Magnetic Resonance (MR) perfusion for determining blood flow. It argues against the prevalent practice of maximizing arterial input levels in the blood flow calculation for a specific echo time (TE). The study highlights the crucial role of the contrast concentration curve noise power, which is intrinsically linked to its maximum value due to the nonlinearity between MR intensity and the contrast concentration. According to the results, when the experimental concentration level and TE are adjusted to produce an MR intensity curve with a signal loss of the contrast MR signal intensity, the optimal signal-to-noise ratio (SNRcc) for a contrast concentration curve can be reached. We demonstrate that the stability of blood flow parameters determined using the singular value decomposition (SVD) deconvolution approach is enhanced with the selected Echo Time setting and contrast to noise ratio (CNR), where the maximum signal loss in the tissue curve. Additionally, deviations from these optimal conditions significantly influence the stability and accuracy of SVD-determined blood flow parameters, depending on the residue function mean transit time. Our research recommends adjusting the experimental TE value to avoid regions of rapidly deteriorating SNRcc in both tissue and arterial curves. This study contributes to the refinement of blood flow determination methods in MR perfusion studies, offering insights for more accurate and stable assessments.

Author Keywords: Signal to Noise Ratio CNR(Contrast-to-Noise ratio)
